courses.title: Days into Gold: Become Creatively Multilingual

instructors.name: Ulysses Chuang
instructors.bio: Ulysses Chuang is an artist, teacher, and lifelong journal keeper. He has studied printmaking in Paris and oil painting in Hong Kong, and his artwork has been exhibited and sold in Hong Kong, Taipei, and Paris. Days into Gold distills what he learned from teaching four Fractal U courses in creative practice: two terms of The Illustrated Journal, as well as Storytelling and Bardic Arts.

courses.description: In Days into Gold, we'll learn to move fluently between writing, drawing, and painting as ways of recording and exploring our lives. Through prompts, timed co-creation, visual storytelling exercises, and a daily illustrated journal practice, we'll cultivate a creative habit that can bring greater depth and savor to the rest of our lives. No previous drawing experience is necessary.

courses.title: Mission-Driven Money: A Practical Fundraising Workshop

instructors.name: Regan Ferrell
instructors.bio: I've worked in the DC think tank world for the last 5 years in various fundraising roles. During this time, I've helped organizations raise over $4.5 million through diverse fundraising strategies. As Development and Operations Manager at Old Pro Productions, I raised $250,000 in one single month during the pandemic to provide emergency support for sex workers facing financial hardship.

courses.description: This hands-on course will equip you with practical skills to fund your social cause, advocacy organization, or policy project. If you've always wondered how to get people excited about and motivated to build a project from the ground up with financial backing, come learn how to do that! We will discover the type of donors that you should pursue, and how you can get them bought into your vision. Over four weeks, you'll learn to: define the right funding sources for your project, develop compelling pitches and proposals, build and leverage your network effectively, and ask for money with confidence.

courses.title: Drum Circle 101

instructors.name: Christian Mortensen
instructors.bio: Hi, my name is Christian and I have loved drumming for as long as I can remember! I have studied and performed in many different styles over the years, including symphonic percussion, marching band, drum set, West African, Afro Latin, Brazilian, and Celtic. Most recently I have had the opportunity to perform with Mambembe Brazilian drum group and The Empire Marching Elite marching band at parades, events, Brooklyn Cyclones games, and even at Radio City Music Hall!

courses.description: Do you want a deeper understanding of rhythm that makes singing, dancing, drumming, and even walking more fun, groovy, and natural? I have just the course for you! In this 7 week rhythmic journey we will explore drumming and percussion in ways that can be applied anywhere – your body, voice, the kitchen table, drums, shakers, pots and pans… your imagination is the limit!

courses.title: Making a Lamp: 3D Modeling, 3D Printing & Design

instructors.name: Mel Brand
instructors.bio: Mel Brand is a Brooklyn-based industrial designer creating environmentally conscious furniture that balances sustainability with playful conceptual thinking. With 10 years of experience in architecture, architectural lighting design, and industrial design her work considers the relationship between furniture, space, and human interaction in the home. She brings levity to complex topics, using humor as a design tool to make serious issues more approachable. Her recent projects span furniture, lighting, and home goods, often working with materials such as wood, 3D printing, ceramics, and fabric. By combining thoughtful design with a systems-oriented mindset, Mel aims to create work that sparks both joy and reflection.

instructors.name: Julianne Lefelhocz
instructors.bio: Julianne Lefelhocz is a multidisciplinary creative technologist and designer merging fashion, design, math, and technology. With over 10 years of experience 3D modeling, two degrees in Computer Science and Footwear and Accessories Design, she is a teacher at the Brooklyn Shoe Space for 3D modeling footwear and a software engineer building CAD tools for jewelry design. She leverages tools such as 3D printing, laser cutting, electronics, kinetics and parametric code to create unique designs for accessories, home goods and fashion. Inspired by the natural world and the mathematical formulas that underpin it, her work often reflects themes of recursion, geometry, and dichotomy.

courses.description: In 6 weeks, learn how to 3D model and design by making a lamp. No experience necessary, this will be an introductory course. We will discuss 3D modeling best practices for 3D printing, as well as making methods.

courses.title: How to Make a Planter: 3D Modeling for 3D Printing

instructors.name: Mel Brand
instructors.bio: Mel Brand is a Brooklyn-based industrial designer creating environmentally conscious furniture that balances sustainability with playful conceptual thinking. With 10 years of experience in architecture, architectural lighting design, and industrial design her work considers the relationship between furniture, space, and human interaction in the home. She brings levity to complex topics, using humor as a design tool to make serious issues more approachable. Her recent projects span furniture, lighting, and home goods, often working with materials such as wood, 3D printing, ceramics, and fabric. By combining thoughtful design with a systems-oriented mindset, Mel aims to create work that sparks both joy and reflection.

instructors.name: Julianne Lefelhocz
instructors.bio: Julianne Lefelhocz is a multidisciplinary creative technologist and designer merging fashion, design, math, and technology. With over 10 years of experience 3D modeling, two degrees in Computer Science and Footwear and Accessories Design, she is a teacher at the Brooklyn Shoe Space for 3D modeling footwear and a software engineer building CAD tools for jewelry design. She leverages tools such as 3D printing, laser cutting, electronics, kinetics and parametric code to create unique designs for accessories, home goods and fashion. Inspired by the natural world and the mathematical formulas that underpin it, her work often reflects themes of recursion, geometry, and dichotomy.

courses.description: Become an emerging 3D modeler from no previous experience and make your own 3D printed planter!

courses.title: Sketchbook Basics: How To Start (and Keep) A Sketchbook Practice

instructors.name: Layla Al Ammari
instructors.bio: Layla Al Ammari (@laylalammari) is an illustrator and artist currently making and learning in NYC. From Bahrain, she is interested in interior and exterior places, and the connection between self and public life. She started with urban sketching, and collage and public life is a big part of her interests and practice. She is currently pursuing her Masters of Fine Arts in Studio Art at Pratt Institute. Guest lecturer Montaysia Yuneek (@byuneek) is an artist and children's book illustrator interested in African American folklore and imaginative space-making. She received her Bachelor of Fine Arts in painting with a minor in African American Studies from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas in 2025, and is currently pursuing her Masters of Fine Arts in Studio Art at Pratt Institute.

courses.dates: Oct 3 – Nov 14 (no class Oct 31 or Nov 7)
courses.description: Sketchbook Basics is a course for anyone interested in starting to engage more with the visual world around them. Part sketchbook, part journal, and part scrapbook, this course carves a space for you to be introduced to different ways of documenting your world, led by two artists. This course is as much about how to draw as it is how to see — what interests you in the world around you?

courses.title: Applied Taijiquan

instructors.name: Michael Weston
instructors.bio: In my 20 years practicing martial arts, including 14 studying Taijiquan, Baguazhang and Xingyiquan, my focus has been on developing all of the benefits Internal Martial Arts (IMAs) have to offer, from the meditative and therapeutic to the more active body skills. This focused pursuit is what I aim to convey through my classes.

courses.description: This class delves into the concepts and practices needed to build practical skill in the martial art of Taijiquan (or Tai Chi Chuan). It focuses on learning in layers to examine the form's nuanced meaning, and training ways to bridge that meaning into detailed body awareness, dynamic problem-solving, and powerful movement literacy.

courses.title: Social Climbers: A Close Reading Series

instructors.name: Elena Navarrete
instructors.bio: Elena studied Comparative Literature and Information Science at Columbia University. For the past two years, she has been leading literary discussion groups in NYC, including a previous group on Anna Karenina. This is her tenth group, following deep dives into East of Eden, One Hundred Years of Solitude, The House of Mirth, The Odyssey, The Brothers Karamazov, and others. She is passionate about incorporating literature into everyday life and building practices that are thoughtful, creative, and alive.

instructors.name: Stephen Thomas
instructors.bio: Stephen Thomas is the author of the story collection The Jokes (2016). He grew up in Canada and has lived all around the world. He co-created Double Double Land, a performance and art space in Kensington Market. He did his MFA at the University of Alabama, taught literature and creative writing there and later at George Brown College, and now lives in New York, where he writes about AI for NYU's Center for Data Science. His fiction has appeared in Joyland, Hobart, Wigleaf, The Puritan, DIAGRAM, and Canadian Art, and his work has been supported by the Edward F. Albee Foundation, the Truman Capote Scholarship Fund, and the Canada Council for the Arts.

courses.description: Over six sessions you will read two novels of social ambition side by side: Balzac's Père Goriot (1835) and Naomi Kanakia's The Default World (2024), following the same figure across two centuries, a poor and clever outsider trying to break into a glittering world. Each week pairs heads-down close reading with discussion, so you leave able to see how a sentence is built, how a scene builds pressure, and what the two books reveal about class, desire, and what it costs to get in.

courses.title: The Hidden Power of Groove: an Intro to Street Dance

instructors.name: Jessica Wang
instructors.bio: Jess Wang is a dancer, movement educator, and former software engineer interested in the relationship between movement, rhythm, embodiment, and self-expression. Drawing from street/club dance styles & choreography including hip hop, house, vogue, waacking, freestyle & kpop, her work explores how expanding one's movement vocabulary can create greater freedom, confidence, connection, and aliveness in everyday life.

courses.location: Dance studio, Manhattan (announced closer to start)
courses.description: Imagine hearing your favorite song come on and feeling excited to jump in instead of wondering what to do. Drawing from street dance styles born on dance floors and at parties (Hip Hop, House, Waacking, and Vogue), this structured beginner class teaches the foundational skills that make dance feel more natural, expressive, and fun. No pressure to "get it right." Just a clear path to building confidence in your body and discovering your own style. Whether you're an absolute beginner, a dancer exploring a new style, or someone simply looking to feel more at home in your body, this class is for you.

courses.title: Intuitive Movement Foundations

instructors.name: Clara Wiest
instructors.bio: Clara Wiest is a Swiss artist, based in NY for 11 years. They are a stage, movement and intimacy director as well as a performance artist. Their whole life has been movement focused; they grew up going to circus school for 12 years, ballet, capoeira, contemporary and modern dance, and they have extensive training in Feldenkrais, Alexander Technique, Clown and Mime, Lucid Body, Qi Gong, somatic practices, hypnotherapy and energy healing, as well as trauma-informed body work.

courses.description: In this course you will be given the space and tools to start creating and/or deepening your relationship to your body. Through somatic exercises, experimental physical theater exercises, Feldenkrais, Alexander technique, Qi Gong practices, parasympathetic nervous system regulation, and breathing, you will learn to take care of your body intuitively. Writing is a part of this practice as well. The goal of this course is that you leave feeling more in tune with yourself, find a sense of play, and leave with tools to keep deepening your relationship with yourself on your own.

courses.title: Exploring Bodywork

instructors.name: Ulysses Chuang
instructors.bio: Ulysses is a certified teacher of the Alexander Technique (ETAPP, Paris, 2014) and has taught it to private students, at ETAPP, in workshops for singers, and in semester-long courses at Fractal University. His musical background includes over a decade of chamber music study with Stéphane Leclerc, a student of Sergiu Celibidache's, as well as voice training with Marc Mauillon, Germana Giannini, and Marine Fribourg. In movement, he has studied Taichi with Aijun Zhang and Yves Blanc, and Kinomichi with Takeharu Noro.

courses.description: Learn to give a session of bodywork to a friend or family member. Taught by Ulysses Chuang in collaboration with Samson Zhilyaev. The optional graduation party takes place in a private Bushwick sauna.

courses.title: Relational Repair

instructors.name: Kez Knopp
instructors.bio: Kez is a trained intimacy coach, focusing on somatic practices and alternative relationships. They have created and facilitated virtual and in-person workshops in New York, San Francisco, and Black Rock City, guiding participants toward honest, embodied ways of relating. By day, Kez works in corporate fintech sales; they understand what it takes to stay grounded and connected when life pulls you toward performance and productivity.

courses.description: Learn to navigate conflict while staying in connection and without compromising yourself or losing the other.

courses.title: Worldbuilding for Storytellers and Narrative Designers

instructors.name: Sarah Guan
instructors.bio: Sarah is an editor and publisher of award-winning speculative fiction. Her authors' work has been nominated for and won many awards, including the Nebula, the Locus, the World Fantasy Award, and the Arthur C. Clarke Award. She has herself been a finalist for the Hugo Award for Best Editor twice. She studied history and literature at Stanford, and thinks about worldbuilding through an interdisciplinary lens.

courses.description: This interdisciplinary seminar explores how fictional worlds operate as structured models of society, drawing on speculative fiction, history, anthropology, and political theory. Students analyze how environments, institutions, culture, memory, and technology shape social order, while building a single evolving fictional world across the semester. The course culminates in a cohesive "world dossier" integrating these elements into a fully realized speculative society that can be used as a platform for creative projects.

courses.title: Poker Strategy

instructors.name: Alex Pinheiro
instructors.bio: Alex Pinheiro is a professional high-stakes online no-limit hold'em player and poker coach based in NYC. In 2023 he completed his bachelor's degree in philosophy at the University of Michigan, specializing in decision theory and Bayesian epistemology. During that time, he studied poker strategy and has played professionally since his graduation.

courses.description: Learn poker strategy from scratch in a rigorous, academic format. Students will have time to play poker and socialize with classmates during each session. No strategy background is assumed, but students must know the rules.

courses.title: Vajrayana: An Introduction

instructors.name: Andrew Blevins
instructors.bio: Andrew Blevins is a writer, coach, and teacher who has practiced contemporary Vajrayana for eight years and meditation more broadly for fifteen. Since 2020, he has been an apprentice in Evolving Ground, a community of Vajrayana practitioners, and since 2023 has hosted the Plant Room Sits, a weekly meditation group in Brooklyn. He has taught courses on approaching Vajrayana, working with emotions, Dzogchen movement, embodied play, creative writing, and loving New York. He writes about human development and other topics on his blog, Immediacy.

courses.description: A six-week experiential introduction to Vajrayana, a Buddhist tradition that emphasizes creativity & transformation in ordinary life. You'll establish a daily meditation practice while exploring Vajrayana approaches to perception, emotion, mantra, ritual, and yidam, with special attention to Tantra and Dzogchen. By the end, you'll have a basic map of the tradition, direct experience with several of its methods, and a sense of whether/how you'd like to pursue it further.

courses.title: Intelligent Partner Training

instructors.name: Zachary Stephens
instructors.bio: Yoga teacher and personal mobility coach with a background in dance, calisthenics, and team sports. Check out MoveInTune.com for more info.

courses.description: Learn how to move with a partner and engage with yourself in ways that improve intimacy, consent, strength, mobility, balance, and coordination. Classes will include a mix of dance, yoga, and calisthenics, with the assistance of props such as bands, sticks, and lacrosse balls, that allow you to move with your partner in ways that are challenging, fun, and safe.

courses.title: Land Is a Big Deal: Georgism and Its Critics

instructors.name: Anthony Rusignuolo
instructors.bio: Tony Rusignuolo grew up in New Jersey and studied civil engineering and computer science. He is a software engineer. He plays volleyball, skates, and snowboards, and he likes ideas.

courses.description: Eight weeks on whether Henry George was right that land should carry the whole tax burden. We read Lars Doucet's Land is a Big Deal against its strongest critics from both the libertarian right and the Marxist left, argue about how much land rent actually exists, and get into the practical question of whether you can even separate the value of a lot from the building on it.

courses.title: Perception, Imagination, Trance

instructors.name: Alicia Botero
instructors.bio: Alicia Botero is a writer and mover from Colombia interested in being part of the wave creating new synthesis between moving and thinking. She is a lover of Contact Improvisation, Qi Gong, Butoh, Tango, Systema, and Salsa; and a dabbler in Pochinko Clowning, Aikido, Gaga, Tai Chi, Body-Mind Centering, Feldenkrais, Alexander Technique… Keen on a comparative approach to understand what movement can do for us, as individuals, communities, and societies, today.

courses.description: Three Tools; a Movement Workshop. Rather than focusing on a particular vocabulary or technique this workshop takes three fundamental tools used across different movement practices: perception, imagination, and trance in order to grant students more learning autonomy, experiential breadth, and insight depth across their practices. Ideal for those who sense movement to be metaphysical, this workshop will dance with the philosophical; we will take support on thinkers of dance and martial arts to enlarge and clarify the possibilities of movement. Expect short readings (to complete before the workshop); solo, partner, and group exercises; a group drink/lunch at the end of each course for longer discussions; and lots of reading and practice recommendations to continue the exploration. Class size: 12. Tuition tiers: $135 basic-level covers space and in-course instruction; $225 general-level aligns with the cost of movement classes in NYC and covers some teaching preparation; $315 supporter-level, based on a $30/hour rate, supports students on scholarship tuition as well as fully compensating the instructor for preparation.

courses.title: How Sentences Work on Us: An Interactive Language Lab

instructors.name: Julia Levine
instructors.bio: Julia Levine is a writer, reader, etymology enthusiast, and ceramicist based in Brooklyn. She earned her bachelor's degree in English and Film from Wesleyan University, where she was editor of Intercut (film journal) and worked under bestselling author Amy Bloom as a Shapiro Writing Center Fellow. Julia has taught and assistant-taught classes across age groups from kindergarteners to adults and graded hundreds of essays for introductory college film courses. She is currently working on a manuscript and occasionally writes a Substack called Veni Vidi Notavi. Julia's love of language is built upon a foundation of seven years studying Latin. Her favorite word is scintilla and she is curious about yours.

courses.location: Penelope House, 16 Prospect Place, North Park Slope, Brooklyn
courses.description: A hybrid classroom-playground for people interested in deepening their relationship with language and finding greater richness in the written word. Over five weeks, we will explore how sentences work on us from a variety of different angles. You can expect something like sentence craft meets linguistic philosophy meets rhetorical/poetic devices meets etymology meets the somatic experience of reading. Every class will feature some combination of lecture, discussion, and interactive writing/reading exercises. Note: this is not a creative writing class, though we will do some writing and some (optional) sharing of our writing as part of our explorations. Avid readers and writers are very welcome to take this class, but reading/writing avidly is not required. Whatever your current relationship with sentences, if this course page sounds interesting, this class is for you. Signups close October 13. Class limited to 16 students, and runs with a minimum of 5.

clubs.name: Claude Squad
clubs.description: Do you like burning calories and burning tokens? Wanna set PRs while merging PRs? Then join the Claude Squad at Vital Williamsburg every other Thursday as we prompt, lift, sauna, and dine together while aura farming and friendshipmogging everyone with our matching outfits! Make no mistake, we're the funnest fitness and computing cult in NYC 💪
clubs.schedule: 6:30 pm, usually every other Thursday. Join the WhatsApp group for dates.

clubs.name: Merlin's Monday Meditation Group
clubs.description: A simple but powerful format: 25 minutes of seated meditation, followed by 25 minutes of silent personal practice — journal, stretch, read, or keep meditating, the choice is yours. A brief sharing circle at the end offers a glimpse into one another's inner worlds, and we close with a few minutes of metta. We've been meeting every Monday for over a year. No RSVP needed and totally free. Just show up.
clubs.schedule: Mondays, 7:30pm. Once a month we host Breaking Bread, a gathering with a large pot of soup for everyone.
